lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Michael, it's Camila from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your body feeling this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay. The heat is getting to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Frozen vegetables count just as much as fresh, and they're cheaper.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the vegetables fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you buy frozen vegetables?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. Vegetables are so expensive right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Healthy food costs a lot.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the vegetables going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the vegetables. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I bought spinach and actually used it. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to feel like yourself again.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly I forgot about it after Tuesday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once the routine broke, it was easy to lose track.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My granddaughter is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. Honestly I forgot about it after Tuesday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 5 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll do it right when I wake up, before anything else.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, so your plan this week is to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 5 days. Did I get that right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Desire to regain energy; coach did not reflect it.
Feels better when sticking to it; daughter support.
Specific days committed; guilt about skipping.
Strong reason: avoiding cancer recurrence; coach pivoted past it.
Asserts a frame about life rather than eliciting.
Wants to keep up with grandkids.
Desire to feel like herself again.
Closed question missed the change talk in line 39.
Late dinners and church are barriers.
Commitment to do it this week.

flags.reason: Coach asserted the meaning of the goal ('getting your life back') instead of eliciting the participant's own reasons after cancer-recurrence concern.
Participant's core motivation ('My granddaughter is why I'm doing this') met a closed question, which pulled toward a yes/no answer and drew out sustain talk.
'I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back' is strong change talk; coach did not reflect or explore it.

score.summary: Coach kept a warm tone and asked permission before advising, and helped the participant set a concrete 5-day goal with barrier planning and a summary. However, several strong change statements (lines 11, 27, 39) were not reflected, and the coach leaned on closed questions and a persuasive reframe (line 28), which reduced partnership.
strengths: Asked permission before sharing an idea (line 8) and repeatedly offered choice (lines 14, 50).
Reflected the participant's desire to feel like herself again (line 35) and the sense of guilt/doubt (line 42).
Ended with a clear plan summary (line 53) and a barrier question (line 51) that led to a concrete routine.
coaching_tips: Reflect the strongest change talk: line 39 'My granddaughter is why I'm doing this' could be answered with 'Your granddaughter really motivates you' instead of a closed question at line 40.
Replace the reframe at line 28 with an open question that asks what the participant thinks matters most about the cancer concern.
Review last week's goal early (missed in this call); ask 'How did the vegetables go since we last talked?' before setting a new goal.
Use more open questions in place of closed ones such as line 44 'Is your daughter able to help?' to explore support in her own words.
